description_full: Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA develops, produces, and distributes medical technology products and components for the people with disabilities in the fields of prosthetics, orthotics, human mobility, and industrial exoskeletons in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North and South America, and the Asia Pacific. The company is involved in identification, development, manufacturing, sales, and marketing of prosthetics, neuro-orthotics, and digital solutions; prostheses for the upper and lower extremities; mechanical prostheses and technologically sophisticated microprocessor-controlled; prosthetic knee joints and feet; arm and hand prostheses; and myoelectrical prostheses activities, as well as socket technologies, including liners, intelligent adaptors, and cosmetic components. It also provides fitting solutions for neurological indications; microprocessor-controlled orthotics, such as the C-Brace; and electrical muscle-activating stimulators, including exopulse suit and conventional orthotics; planning and equipping of patient care clinics; solutions for back, shoulder, neck, and wrist; customized orthopedic treatment and rehabilitation solutions; manual and power wheel chair; and standing aids and cushions, as well as care for amputees, including peripheral artery disease, traumatic limb loss, cancer, infections, congenital limb deficiencies, etc; and neurological etiologies, including stroke, multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy/spinal cord injury, etc. In addition, the company leases out products, including wheelchairs and microprocessor-controlled knee joints. Ottobock SE & Co. was formerly known as Otto Bock HealthCare GmbH and changed its name to Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA in April 2018. The company was founded in 1919 and is based in Duderstadt, Germany. Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA operates as a subsidiary of Näder Upside 2 Vermögensverwaltungs GmbH.

financial_summary: Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $4.0B market cap on $1.9B of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 53% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $250M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.69× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.9×.

Net dilution runs at 2.4% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 14% operating margin runs 14pp above the Healthcare median (0%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.58x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 458 companies in the universe; the top four hold 35% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
val: The stock trades 60% below its DCF fair value of $31.50, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 59%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $20.47 to $49.90 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Healthcare peers: EV/EBITDA 5.9 vs 15.7 and P/FCF 16.1 vs 23.7 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 6.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 13.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 1.1% annual cash-flow growth, 16pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 2pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar.
It runs a 53% gross margin and converts 13% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 3.69x, but a weak Piotroski score of 3/9 and high accruals (-11.9% of assets).
ROE of 23% is amplified by 5.3x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

The current ratio of 0.95 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-2.4%), diluting holders.
people: With about 9,406 employees, each generates about $199K of revenue, 0.5x the Healthcare median.
